chunks: And from him, from al-Nadhr, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding at what distance a man shortens his prayer. He said, 'At the distance of a day's travel or two Bair (units of distance).' He added, 'For indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) went out to Dhi Khushub and shortened (his prayer).' I asked, 'How far is Dhi Khushub?' He said, 'Two Bair.'

key_terms.بَيَاضِ يَوْمٍ: The distance of a day's travel

ai.seo_question: What is the specific distance in Islamic jurisprudence that qualifies a person as a traveler for shortening prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific geographical threshold for the traveler's prayer concession, defining it as two Bair (approximately 40-42 km), a standard widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence. By citing the Prophet’s journey to Dhi Khushub, the Imam anchors this legal ruling in prophetic precedent, distinguishing the practical application of qasr from the more general concept of 'bayadhi yawm'. This establishes a clear, measurable criterion for Muslims to determine when they transition from resident to traveler status regarding prayer and fasting.
